column1: # Reviewed exceptions for scrub_sweep.py on the public LOKA Pay repo.
# Format: <pattern_id><TAB><path glob relative to the repo root><TAB><sha256 of the exact
# matched value>. A rule allows ONE value of ONE pattern in matching paths: any other
# value, even in the same file, still fails. Values never appear here, only their hashes.
# Hashes were computed by a read-only sweep of the original LOKA v0.6.66 tree
# (commit 3377240a, the files that survive the scrub, post-move paths). To add a rule,
# run the sweep with --suggest-allowlist OUT, review each candidate, copy it here.
# Every rule must name a value that the public tree itself carries: a plain hash of a
# short value (serial, team id, email) can be brute-forced. Never add a rule for a value
# the scrub removes. The import publishes only the rules its tree uses, and audits them.
# Font designer contact inside the SIL Open Font License text (attribution the license requires).
# Unit-test phone numbers, all in the reserved fictional 555 range.
# Protocol test vectors and the test that reads them: SHA-256 hashes of fixed test data.
# Payment vectors written during the event (note ids are SHA-256 hex by design) are added
# here value by value, after review, with --suggest-allowlist. No path-wide exception.
# A documentation URL whose path has a "home" segment; it is not a home directory.
# Public phone model numbers in written reports. These name a product, not a device.
# The sweep tool names the pattern it searches for.
# Bluetooth protocol constants that ship in source and in protocol/BLE-LINK-V1.md: LOKA's BLE
# service and characteristic UUIDs, the standard Bluetooth SIG CCCD descriptor UUID, and the
# Bluetooth Classic service id. Protocol constants, not device identifiers.
# Synthetic test fixture ids (repeated digits or 12345678-...) in unit tests and a protocol vector.
# Public citations: a library record id in a cited dspace.mit.edu URL, and the public commit of
# an open-source project that two LOKA reviews pin.
# The same font designer contact inside the two Lilita One font files (the font's own name table).
# Content Credentials (C2PA) ids inside AI-generated PNG art: the manifest label and the XMP
# instance id that the image generator embeds. Per-image provenance ids, not device or user ids.
